jobs.title: Hospice Social Worker (MSW)
jobs.description:
Are you a compassionate, dedicated professional looking to make a meaningful impact in the lives of patients and their families during their most vulnerable moments? Join the Bristol Hospice team as a **Hospice Social Worker**, where your work will play a critical role in providing comfort, support, and dignity to those nearing the end of life.  



Bristol Hospice is a nationwide industry leader committed to providing a family\-centered approach in the delivery of hospice services throughout our communities. We are dedicated to our mission that all patients and families entrusted to our care will be treated with the highest level of compassion, respect, and dignity. For more information about Bristol Hospice, visit bristolhospice.com or follow us on LinkedIn.  



**Schedule:** Monday\-Friday, 8am\-5pm




**Coverage Area:** Denver \& surrounding areas




**Our Culture**


Our culture is cultivated using the following values:

* **Integrity:** We are honest and professional.
* **Trust:** We count on each other.
* **Excellence:** We strive to always do our best and look for ways to improve and excel.
* **Accountability:** We accept responsibility for our actions, attitudes, and mistakes.
* **Mutual Respect:** We treat others the way we want to be treated.

**An Average Day:**  

*(Includes, but not limited to)*

* Assess the psychosocial status of patients and families/caregivers related to the patient's terminal illness and environment and communicates findings to the registered nurse and other members of the interdisciplinary group
* Provide an assessment in the patient's identified residence and assistance when this is not safe, and another plan is required
* Carry out social evaluations, including family dynamics, caregiver abilities, communication patterns, high risks for suicide, neglect or abuse and plan intervention based on evaluation findings
* Counsel patient and family/caregivers as needed in relationship to stress, and other identified coping difficulties; provide crisis intervention when necessary
* Assess for, and educate interdisciplinary group, on any special needs related to the culture of the patient and family, including communication, role of family, space, and any special traditions or taboos
* Maintain clinical records on all patients referred to social work
* Educate patients and families on, and assist in, preparation of advanced directives
* Provide information and referral services for organization patients and families/caregivers regarding practical and environmental needs
* Provide information to patients and families/caregivers and community agencies
* Serve as liaison between patients and families/caregivers and community agencies
* Maintain collaborative relationships with organization personnel to support patient care
* Maintain and develop contacts with public and private agencies as resources for patient and personnel
* Participate in the development of the individualized plan of care, involving the patient and family, and attend regularly scheduled interdisciplinary group meetings, assist the team in recognizing the effects of the psychosocial stresses on symptoms of the terminal illness
* Assist physician and other team members in understanding significant social and emotional factors related to health problems and death/dying issues
* Actively participate in quality assessment performance improvement teams and activities
* Assist family and patient in planning for funeral arrangements, financial, legal, and health care decision responsibilities
* Perform other duties as delegated by the Clinical Supervisor




**Requirements:**

* Must have a master’s degree in social work from an accredited university.
	+ If you hold an undergraduate B.A, Degree in Social Work, you are eligible to apply. Please know the hirable rate of pay will be based on degree type.
* Must have minimum of two (2\) years of documented supervised experience in health care, hospice experience preferred
* Must understand hospice philosophy, and issues of death/dying.
* Certified Hospice and Palliative Social Worker is desirable
* Must be flexible in work hours and have the ability to travel throughout the assigned Bristol Hospice service area
* Must demonstrate a willingness to maintain comprehensive working knowledge regarding information systems and applicable software programs




**We Got the Perks:**

* Tuition Reimbursement
* PTO and Paid Holidays
* Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, and more
* HSA \& 401(k) available
* Mileage Reimbursement for applicable positions
* Advanced training programs
* Passionate company culture committed to the highest standard of care in the hospice industry




***Join a Team that embraces the reverence of life!***

*Bristol Hospice is an equal\-opportunity employer. Our success depends upon our ability to create and maintain a diverse and supportive work environment where individuality is promoted. Bristol puts high priority on the worth of every person. **Position:** Care Coordination Program Manager
**Reports To:** Senior Manager, National Training
**Department:** Child First Clinical
**Supervisory Role:** No
**Location:** Remote, U.S.
**Employment Status:** Full\-Time
  

**FLSA Status:** Exempt  

**POSITION OVERVIEW**
The Care Coordination Program Manager supports all training efforts in service of Child First implementing partner organizations (IPO). This role requires facilitation and cofacilitation of training to develop, strengthen and sustain the Child First program practitioners’ knowledge and understanding of the model to support implementation with fidelity. This position is responsible for codeveloping and establishing sustainability efforts within workforce development that are in the best interest of a healthy and sustainable Child First network. This position will have the opportunity to engage in organizational efforts focused on enhancing Child First model implementation, practice integrity, quality enhancement, as well as equity and inclusion.
Additionally, this position will support organizational initiatives within the infant and early childhood mental health national community focused on thought leadership and innovation.  

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES \& RESPONSIBILITIES**
**60% Training Development and Delivery**
* Facilitate and/or cofacilitates live\-remote and in\-person training sessions as necessary to support the Child First network.
* Leads model\-specific consultation calls supporting model implementation.
* Supports the Child First Training team within the learning management system for session registrations, attendance, and other necessary reports/projects.
* Co\-leads development of training agendas and updates to and utilization of training resources systems (i.e., Padlet) for Child First trainings.
* Engages in continuous improvement of training curricula (e.g., ongoing evaluation and updating of training materials, ensuring content remains current, evidence\-informed, and responsive to policy or model changes).
* Reviews and evaluates training feedback and collaborates on the development and implementation of quality improvement plans for training sessions/materials based on feedback.
  

**30% Subject Matter Expertise \& Cross\-Collaboration**
* Engages across the organization to bring subject matter expertise into cross\-functional groups, committees, and initiatives (e.g., early relational health, racial and social justice, and reflective practice).
* Engages in organizational projects to assess IECMH training needs of communities, pilot new approaches, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and community needs. Develop training products, workshops, and technical assistance offerings to external partners as warranted.
* Represent the organization as a subject matter expert by presenting at conferences, building partnerships, and promoting the home visiting model and training expertise to new audiences

  

**10% Administrative Support, Team Engagement, and Technical Expertise**  

* Engages with the Child First programs learning management system in service to Child First and utilize educational software in conjunction with instructional design team.
* Actively participates in Clinical\-Training team and cross\-collaborative groups in service to network health and sustainability.
* Participate in larger organizational meetings, Child First departmental meetings, and individual supervision regularly.
  

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, \& EXPERIENCE**
* Bachelor’s degree in social work, psychology, human development and family studies, early childhood education, public health, counseling, sociology, or equivalent experience.
* Minimum 2 years’ experience working in the role of Child First Care Coordinator required.
* Demonstrated knowledge of infant and early childhood development, including social\-emotional development and early relational health, and core principles of infant and early childhood mental health (IECMH)
* Strong understanding of the Child First model , including key components, clinical frameworks, and expectations for high\-fidelity implementation
* Experience developing and delivering trainings using adult learning principles, with strong facilitation skills in both in\-person and virtual settings
* Ability to translate complex clinical concepts into clear, practical guidance that supports skill\-building and application in the field
* Knowledge of reflective practice and experience supporting relationship\-based work with practitioners and teams
* Experience working with diverse families, with a commitment to culturally responsive, strengths\-based, and trauma\-informed approaches
* Strong project management, organizational, and problem\-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and troubleshoot system and workflow issues
* Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to engage multidisciplinary teams and build effective working relationships
* Experience supporting implementation, coaching, or continuous quality improvement efforts within home visiting, early childhood, or behavioral health settings
* Travel as necessary (estimated 20% of the time), dependent on current public health conditions and business need.
  

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**
This position reports to Senior Manager, National Training and has no direct reports.

**This role is a fully remote position. MUST BE LOCATED IN A STATE WE OFFER DEVOTED.**

***A bit about this role:***


As a Transitions of Care (TOC ) Behavioral Health Social Worker, you will focus on Transitions of Care (TOC) support for Devoted members. You will provide short term interventions to members in the process of being connected to community based behavioral health services, either because of an emerging need or following a hospitalization. The goal is to prevent avoidable emergency room/inpatient care and/or prevent readmission to the hospital.


The TOC team is dedicated to providing culturally competent care with a focus on equity and quality. We pay close attention to our team culture, treating each other like family so we have the requisite resiliency to care for our members like family.

***Required skills and experience:***

* Master’s degree in Social Work with an active clinical license in any US state \- LCSW, LMSW, or comparable state clinical license. Willingness to gain additional state licenses.
* Minimum of 5 years experience in the behavioral health or care management fields
* Competent performing comprehensive psychosocial assessments over video and phone
* Able to independently manage a fully remote work schedule, M\-F, 8:30am\-5:00pm PST or MST

***Desired skills and experience:***

* Bilingual in English and Spanish, Creole or Vietnamese preferred, but not required
* Experience in Geriatric BH or the health insurance industry (Medicare Advantage is a big plus)

***Your Responsibilities will include:***

* Performing comprehensive psychosocial assessments via phone/video with members and caregivers
* Conduct clinical social work interventions to maximize the effectiveness of the program including: brief therapeutic interventions, assistance in navigating family/support issues, assessing and intervening on social determinants of health, completing safety assessments
* Interdisciplinary collaboration with teammates (including clinicians, nurses, and care coordinators) to ensure cohesive, patient\-centered care for high\-needs patients
* Ability to clinically identify and escalate complex members to the BH Medical Director for consultation
